name: Sofia Ayala
life: “I still remember the day we finally owned the house clean and clear.” On Sunday, near the corner outside Coastal Barber, Sofia usually checks the board before the regulars give a more colorful account of the news.
voice: I understand every page I signed. I would like the children to stop treating my generosity as a symptom.
appearance: Sofia is easy to recognize by steel-colored hair cut square above the collar and a flat bridge to the nose and a mobile brow. Usually dressed in a dark green knitted vest with a printed handkerchief folded into the pocket, Sofia rubs a thumb along the edge of the nearest pocket when listening.
personality: Sofia loves a well-told anecdote and distrusts the neat ending. The parts Sofia remembers are the interruptions, unfinished jobs and people who had to go back to work halfway through.
agenda: To keep authority over the guarantee personally signed.
family: Louis Law is Sofia’s younger cousin. Sofia offers the first invitation. Louis gets to change the plan. They learned that a promise to visit is easier to keep when changing a time does not count as letting down the whole family. Asked about *The driving lesson fund*, Louis says, “I teach under pressure for a living. I want my learner to get through one bend without apologizing for taking time.”
connections: Sonia Arnett (daughter). Daughter and mother have to discuss different meanings of a generous guarantee.
